about: The steps of Horde's first run on a machine, in order: the one source of what Horde needs. cli/Setup.ps1 interprets it (horde setup); each id has its check, and its fix when it has one, in that file. A later change generates the README's first-run section and the installer from it. In manual, {relay}, {origin}, {home}, {root}, {machine}, {label} and {elevated} are filled in by horde setup.

steps.title: what Horde needs
steps.requirement: Windows 10 or 11, and Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe), which comes with Windows; Git for Windows to get Horde
steps.checks: Windows is version 10 or later, powershell.exe 5.1 is installed, and setup is running under it
steps.fixes: when started from PowerShell 7, setup runs itself again under Windows PowerShell 5.1
steps.manual: run horde from Windows PowerShell 5.1: powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File {root}\horde.ps1 setup

steps.title: Microsoft Store automatic updates off
steps.requirement: the Microsoft Store does not update apps by itself: a Store update closes every running process of the package, and on 2026-10-16 one closed every pwsh.exe and every session with it (CONTRIBUTING 16)
steps.fixes: sets that value to 2 when this prompt is elevated; never elevates by itself, and from a prompt that is not elevated says so in one sentence and sets nothing
steps.manual: run horde setup again from a PowerShell window opened as administrator: it sets HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\WindowsStore AutoDownload to 2

steps.title: PowerShell 7 from the MSI, not the Microsoft Store
steps.requirement: PowerShell 7 installed from the vendor's MSI at C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe, which Horde starts by full path; Horde never depends on a Microsoft Store package
steps.checks: pwsh.exe from the MSI is installed and reports a version; when the pwsh on the search path is the Store copy (under a WindowsApps folder), that is noted
steps.fixes: when the MSI copy is missing and this prompt is elevated, takes the MSI's address and SHA-256 from winget show, downloads it to a fresh temporary folder, checks the SHA-256, installs it quietly with msiexec (no automatic updates through Microsoft Update), and checks that the new pwsh.exe reports its version; never uninstalls the Store copy, which would close every pwsh.exe running from it
steps.manual: run horde setup again from a PowerShell window opened as administrator: it installs the PowerShell 7 MSI

steps.title: Horde home
steps.requirement: a folder of Horde's own: HORDE_HOME, or .horde in the user's profile

steps.title: the hosted relay's own steps
steps.requirement: for a home that hosts its own relay: where it will answer, its Google sign-in client and the tools it is deployed with
steps.checks: each of the relay's own steps, as the relay says them (relays/<name>/Setup.ps1): its origin, its Google sign-in client file with the exact redirect URI and JavaScript origin to register, node
steps.manual: do what the relay's step above says

steps.title: relay deployed
steps.requirement: the operator's relay is deployed, serving the phone app
steps.checks: a deploy from this home recorded the origin the relay will answer at

steps.title: relay settings
steps.requirement: the relay settings name this machine's horde and where the phone app is
steps.checks: settings\relay.json names horde, pairRpId and pairOrigin
steps.fixes: writes settings\relay.json, in ASCII, when it is not there: the horde named by -Horde (home by default), and the phone app at the relay this home uses
steps.manual: horde setup -Horde <a name for this horde: a-z, 0-9 and -, such as home>

steps.title: machine identity
steps.requirement: this machine's relay identity: its keys, made in this machine's key store (the TPM when there is one) and never copied
steps.checks: an identity record exists in the Horde home
steps.fixes: makes it, as horde relay identity -New does

steps.title: relay runner defined
steps.requirement: the relay runner - what carries questions to the phone and answers back - defined as a service of this home, so the supervisor can keep it running
steps.checks: settings\service-definitions.json has a service that runs horde relay run for this home
steps.fixes: writes settings\service-definitions.json, in ASCII, when it is not there
steps.manual: add the relay-runner entry setup prints to settings\service-definitions.json

steps.title: relay runner kept running
steps.requirement: the supervisor scheduled for this home, so the relay runner runs from start-up without a window left open
steps.checks: both of the supervisor's jobs are installed, enabled, made by Horde, and serve this home
steps.fixes: installs them, as horde services schedule does, when this prompt is elevated; never elevates by itself
steps.manual: in any PowerShell window, run this one line, and allow it to run as administrator: {elevated}

steps.title: relay runner serving
steps.requirement: the relay runner running for this home
steps.checks: the relay runner's heartbeat is fresh and says it can do its work
steps.fixes: none: a long-running process is started by the person or by the supervisor, never by setup
steps.manual: horde relay run -Relay {relay}, and leave that window open

steps.title: phone paired
steps.requirement: a phone signed in to the relay and paired with this machine
steps.checks: the trust store holds a phone that is trusted
steps.fixes: runs the pairing, as horde relay pair -Relay {relay} does: shows the QR code and the offer, says where to tap on the phone, waits for the phone, then asks for the 12-digit number the phone shows and compares it; Google sign-in itself happens on the phone
steps.manual: on the phone, open {origin}/app/index.html, sign in with Google, add it to the home screen and open it from there; then here: horde relay pair -Relay {relay} -Label "{label}", and in the app: Pair with a machine, Scan the QR code; then type the 12-digit number the phone shows

steps.title: test question
steps.requirement: a first question on the decisions list, to see it reach the phone
steps.checks: the decisions list holds the question horde setup adds, in the group Setup
steps.fixes: adds it once: Horde is set up on {machine} - does it reach your phone?
steps.manual: horde decisions add -File <a question file>, as horde setup would
